analysis: The change adds a single test file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Benchmark/RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmarkTests.swift (lines 1-234). It covers benchmark plan validation: batch-size parsing, staggered quota math, a MiMo refusal, row finish-reason validation, median summary, report provenance, and a drain-while-submitting ordering test. It contains no production code, no network, key or attestation handling, and no changes to the TB-002 or TB-003 trust boundaries. Fixtures are public ("Public fixture", a temporary config.json holding only model_type). The MiMo test writes to FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory under a UUID-named directory and removes it in a defer. This holds only synthetic public data, so it does not relate to the T-050 plaintext temp-file concern. The test imports ProviderCore through @_spi(Benchmarking) @testable. This adds no runtime attack surface, because test-only code is not shipped in the provider binary, though that depends on SPI/target configuration outside the supplied evidence. The non-test RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark and ProviderBenchmark implementations are not in this batch. Integration should check whether the Benchmarking SPI exposes anything in the release product, and whether the benchmark executable can load a user-supplied modelDirectory and write reports. I found no concrete security regression or threat-model gap from this file alone.
